objectives.title: Amend the greybox so it fits the exterior model's measured dimensions (greybox v4)
objectives.why_score: Named a must by the creator; every other interior objective stands on a footprint that actually fits inside the exterior walls. Not 9 because a misfit is invisible until the player walks into a wall or out through one.
objectives.detail: Read the v3 alignment JSON (scale 34.30 from the original GLB, tower centre (3.5, 3.6), main house centre (-3.73, 4.89) and long axis, ground floor y 0.97, basement floor y -2.0, lantern floor y 17.9, measured entry door at (-3.494, 0.97, 8.874) with its normal) and the exterior mesh. Build lighthouse_greybox_v4.glb plus a v4 alignment JSON: wall thickness tapering up the tower, the house footprint inside the exterior shell, the door opening matching the measured door, and floors at the measured heights. Fix what the v3 alignment file itself warns about: the exterior mesh has a solid house-to-tower wall that needs carving or collision regeneration, so the route from house to tower is not walkable yet. Keep v3 as the safe fallback.
acceptance: lighthouse_greybox_v4.glb and its alignment JSON exist
every interior wall lies inside the exterior shell with a stated margin
the entry door opening matches the measured door within tolerance
v3 is kept unchanged

objectives.title: Build the slice-critical rooms from the blueprint: entry vestibule and hallway, stairs down, boiler room, tower stair, lantern room
objectives.why_score: These are the rooms the GDD beats use: Ted opens the door, the coal job in the boiler room, the tower climb, the lantern diagnosis and the burner fit. Not 9 because without them the slice cannot be played.
objectives.detail: From the Interior Plan V4 blueprint: G entry vestibule, hallway (posters and documents) and stairs down to the basement; B1 boiler room (shovel coal here), coal store, steam engine and dynamo; the tower stair (spiral) up to L3; L3 lantern gallery, arc lamp (broken at start) and maintenance space. Build to the blueprint's relative sizes and adjacencies, scaled to the v4 footprint, in greybox with clear volumes and doorways. Anything the blueprint does not show is marked as an addition for the creator to approve.
acceptance: each listed room exists in the v4 greybox and matches the blueprint adjacency
the coal-to-lantern route is continuous
additions beyond the blueprint are listed

checks.note: Compare each room against the blueprint legend.

objectives.title: Prove the interior route is walkable: collision, headroom, step height, no blocked doors
objectives.why_score: A blocked route stops the slice and the v3 alignment file says it is not certified walkable. Not 9 because the player cannot proceed at all if it fails.
objectives.detail: Generate collision for the v4 greybox (box or convex per part, not one giant trimesh). Write tools/test_interior_route.gd that walks the Player capsule door to hall to basement to tower stair to lantern room and fails on any block. Respect the player movement spec: step-up 0.4 m, floor angle 60 degrees; stair rise and run must fit inside it with headroom for the camera.
acceptance: tools/test_interior_route.gd exists and passes headless 8 of 8 runs
stair rise <= step-up limit; every doorway clears the capsule and camera

checks.note: Run the route test and walk it.

objectives.title: Prove the two GDD sightlines: the window to the dock and rowboat, and the lamp room to the ship route and island rock
objectives.why_score: GDD decisions 22 and 26 make these load-bearing for two story beats and the fail presentation. Not 10 because the route (LHI-03) must exist first.
objectives.detail: Place a window in the right room facing the dock and the rowboat mooring, and lamp-room windows all around with one view on the rock where the ship passes or crashes. Verify with a ray or camera check from the player eye height, in the v4 greybox in Level.tscn.
acceptance: from the window position a ray reaches the rowboat mooring unobstructed
from the lamp room a ray reaches the ship-route rock unobstructed

checks.note: Run the sightline check and look from both windows in Godot.

objectives.title: Apply real lighthouse design to the interior: tapering walls, spiral stair with landing windows, lantern gallery, service levels below
objectives.why_score: The creator asked for an agent that knows lighthouse design. Not 10 because the greybox is a blockout and realism is secondary to the route.
objectives.detail: Walls thick at the base and thinner at the top; a spiral stair around the tower core with a landing and small window every few turns; the lantern room on top with a surrounding gallery and a door onto it; engine, coal and stores below the entry floor; keeper's living space and the control level between. Record each design choice against the blueprint so the creator can see what is real-world lighthouse practice and what is from the plan.
acceptance: a design note maps each choice to the blueprint or to lighthouse practice
stair has landings and windows at regular heights

objectives.title: Fit the interior lights inside the dynamic-light budget, with the Lighting agent
objectives.why_score: The scene already has 16 interior OmniLight3D nodes; the GDD budgets dynamic lights around the beacon and key hazards. Not 9 because lighting is already working.
objectives.detail: Baseline: Level.tscn has 15 interior OmniLight3D nodes (entry hall, basement, eight spiral-stair lights, the lantern) against a lighting_spec budget of max_dynamic_lights 8 and 2 shadow casters. Unless a script culls them by proximity the budget is exceeded. Compare light count and positions with the budget and decide per room which become baked or fake lighting. Per-room mood from the lore: dim, claustrophobic halls; warm firebox glow in the boiler room; the arc lamp the only strong source when lit. Use baked or cheap fake lighting for rooms the player is not in.
acceptance: no more than 8 interior dynamic lights are live at once (or the creator raises the budget)
per-room mood checked by capture

objectives.title: Add interaction anchors and set dressing markers: boiler, coal, door, window, arc lamp, burner socket, posters
objectives.why_score: Other agents' tasks (coal job, lantern diagnosis, burner fit) need fixed places to attach to. Not 9 because anchors are cheap once the rooms exist.
objectives.detail: Marker3D anchors named by role in the v4 scene. Posters and documents praising the moon cycle and the Flighted (pillar and lore) as placeholder quads in the hallway. No story is added.
acceptance: anchors exist and are listed for the Gameplay / Systems agent

objectives.title: Decide how far the upper floors go for the prototype: walk-through shells or sealed floors with stair landings
objectives.why_score: The blueprint has L1 (keeper's quarters) and L2 (control and diagnostics) between the entry floor and the lantern room; the slice route only needs the stair through them. Not higher because there is a safe default.
objectives.detail: Option A: build L1 and L2 as enterable greybox shells with their rooms. Option B: seal them, with a door and a landing on the stair, and build only the lantern room and the route. Option C: A for L2 (control, diagnostics) and B for L1. Cost rises with each room built and tested.
acceptance: the creator has chosen A, B or C
objectives.decision: Walk-through L1 and L2 (A), sealed with landings (B), or L2 only (C)? Recommendation: C, because L2 holds the diagnostics story and L1 can follow after the slice.

checks.note: Creator picks A, B or C.

acceptance: comparison note exists
offline asset check passes
